question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy

| Source | Returned count/status | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** | **3 matches** | Three records matched the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy search. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | The count does not establish verified human pregnancy outcomes, distinct studies, evidence quality, or what any record found. No abstracts or findings were retrieved. The query’s daridorexant MeSH term was not found. |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** | **4 registration matches** | Four trial-registration records matched `daridorexant AND (pregnancy)`. [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) | The count does not establish posted results, enrollment, outcomes, or confirmed applicability to a particular pregnancy population or age band. |
| **DailyMed** | **1 name-matched product label** | One DailyMed label record matched the medicine name. [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) | The count does not establish that the label contains pregnancy-specific evidence, current approval status, or independent clinical evidence. |
| **LactMed** | **Not applicable; no count returned** | LactMed was not counted because it is lactation-only. | This is not a zero and does not establish absence of pregnancy evidence. LactMed is not a pregnancy evidence source. [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** | **0 rows; 0 distinct PMIDs** | No literal daridorexant-name row matches were found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot tables. Snapshot date: **2026-11-17**; revision `4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89`. [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) | This does not establish that no relevant study exists. The returned limit is literal drug-name matching in selected snapshot tables, without name resolution or a full-portal search; rows are not distinct studies. |

These are presence/count-navigation results only. The returned MCP notice states that counts are not comparable across sources and cannot establish evidence quality, clinical safety, or study findings. A zero or unavailable result may reflect query, indexing, snapshot, or population limits; it is not evidence of safety. No full evidence records were retrieved.

The MCP also reports that its prototype source review did not identify a curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed; this is a source-review limitation, not proof that no such resource exists. [S5](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/labeling/questions-and-answers-pregnancy-and-lactation-labeling-rule) [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/)

The MCP’s continuity-of-care notice states that stopping or changing a medication can also carry risks and should be discussed with the prescribing clinician.
